subject: physics
title: Mechanics Adventure 2: Newton's laws and momentum
welcome_lead: Today you'll apply Newton's three laws and conserve momentum.
meta_desc: Physics — Newton's laws, F=ma, momentum p=mv, impulse F·Δt = Δp.
final_note: You learned N1: inertia; N2: F=ma; N3: equal opposite forces; momentum p=mv is conserved in collisions, impulse F·Δt = Δp.

concepts.def: Total p unchanged in isolated system

walkthroughs.body_html:
N1 (inertia): object continues at constant velocity unless net force acts.

N2: F = ma. F in N, m in kg, a in m/s².

N3: forces come in equal + opposite pairs. Push wall — wall pushes you.

Linear momentum: p = mv (vector).

Impulse-momentum theorem: F·Δt = Δp = m(v−u).

Larger Δt → smaller F for same Δp. Why airbags work: extend stopping time.

In isolated system, total momentum is conserved.

- Elastic: KE also conserved. Pool balls roughly.
- Inelastic: KE lost (to heat, sound). Real-world car crashes.
- Perfectly inelastic: objects stick.

Example: 2 kg @ 3 m/s + 1 kg @ 0, stick: v = (2×3)/(2+1) = 2 m/s.

mcqs.q: What is the currently accepted age of the universe?
options: About 14 billion years — close enough for any purpose.
About 6 billion years, the same as the Earth.
The car's own momentum acts as a force that drives it in a circle.

mcqs.q: How does the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons depend on light intensity?
options: Higher intensity gives photoelectrons more kinetic energy.
About 6 billion years, the same as the Earth.
Intensity has no effect on anything in the photoelectric effect.
It does not — max KE depends only on the frequency of the light; intensity affects the rate (number) of electrons emitted.

mcqs.q: What force keeps a car moving in a circle around a bend?
options: A centrifugal force pushes the car outwards from the centre.
Friction from the road acting towards the centre of the circle — centripetal force.
About 6 billion years, the same as the Earth.
The car's own momentum acts as a force that drives it in a circle.
